start.title: A dream
start.text:
You wake sometime in the night.

At first, you do not know what disturbed you. The room is almost completely dark, save for a thin wash of moonlight leaking through the curtains and silvering the edge of the floor. Your sheets are warm and tangled around you, one arm still buried beneath the pillow where you must have fallen asleep. The air carries the faint coolness that settles into the palace after midnight, enough to make the warmth of the bed feel particularly difficult to leave.

For a while, you simply lie there. Sleep has not entirely released you, and the room seems to exist only in fragments: the dim outline of the wardrobe, the pale suggestion of the dressing mirror, the darker shape of the balcony curtains against the wall. Nothing appears out of place. Nothing immediately explains why you are awake.

You close your eyes again, expecting whatever restless thought pulled you from sleep to pass. It does not.
Somewhere beneath the lingering heaviness of sleep, there is the quiet certainty that something is different.

choices.flavourText: The palace is silent.

d02.title: A dream
d02.text:
Not frightening. Not yet. Just wrong in the way a familiar room can sometimes seem unfamiliar when seen at an unusual hour.

Usually, even at night, there is life somewhere beyond your door: the muted tread of a guard passing along the corridor, servants changing shifts, the distant splash of water in the gardens below. Small sounds you have heard so often that you rarely notice them.

Tonight, there is nothing.

No footsteps.

No voices.

Not even wind against the balcony doors.

You hold your breath and listen harder, as though the palace might reveal itself if you are patient enough.

choices.flavourText: The world arrives slowly.

d03.title: A dream
d03.text:
Your eyes adjust slowly to the darkness. Familiar shapes emerge around you: the chair beside the bed, the low table near the window, the dressing mirror catching a pale sliver of moonlight. Nothing seems disturbed, yet the feeling that woke you refuses to fade.

You listen again, half-expecting the palace to reassert itself. A guard should pass eventually. Somewhere below, water should still be moving through the gardens. Instead there is only the same heavy silence.
Then your gaze settles on the door.
It is open.

Only slightly. A narrow strip of darkness between the door and its frame.

You are almost certain you closed it before sleeping.

choices.flavourText: Your voice slips into the dark. Nothing answers.
The warmth of the sheets gives way to cold stone beneath your feet.
The silence begins to feel less like an absence of sound and more like something being held.

d04.title: A dream
d04.text:
The palace remains silent.

Beyond your door, the corridor is washed in thin moonlight. The lamps along the walls are unlit, and the long stretch of polished stone disappears into shadow at either end. Nothing moves.

That is strange enough on its own.

At this hour there should still be guards somewhere nearby. There should be servants crossing between the inner rooms, or at least the distant sound of someone awake where they ought not to be.

Instead, the corridor feels abandoned.

Even the air seems still.

And then, somewhere farther along the hall, a door slowly swings shut.

choices.flavourText: The sound gives the silence a direction.
The words travel farther than they should. No familiar voice answers them.

choices.text: Wait and see if anything else moves.
choices.flavourText: The silence stretches with you.

d05.title: A dream
d05.text:
The corridor seems longer once you begin paying attention to it.

Not dramatically so. There is no impossible stretching of walls, no sudden transformation. The pillars remain where you remember them, the same tapestries hang between the windows, and the same pale stone runs beneath your feet.

And yet the door at the far end does not seem any closer.

Moonlight lies across the floor in narrow bands. Between them, the darkness feels deeper than it should, swallowing the familiar details of the palace until each stretch of corridor seems briefly unfamiliar.

Then something catches your eye beside one of the windows.

A mark on the floor.

Too dark to be moonlight. Too irregular to be part of the stone.

From here, you cannot quite tell what it is.

choices.flavourText: Up close, the darkness has a sheen to it.
The glass is cold beneath your fingertips.

choices.text: Leave it and keep following the corridor.
choices.flavourText: Some mysteries are easier to follow than others.

d04_wait_01.title: A dream
d04_wait_01.text:
Nothing follows.

The corridor settles again beneath the moonlight. No shadow crosses the floor. No guard rounds the corner. Whatever closed the distant door seems content to leave you wondering.

You remain where you are.

After a while, you become aware of how loud your own breathing sounds.

choices.flavourText: Stillness becomes its own kind of attention.
Waiting has revealed nothing.

d05_wait_02.title: A dream
d05_wait_02.text:
Another stretch of silence passes.

Your eyes begin finding details they missed before: the slight movement of a curtain, a pale edge of moonlight beneath a chair, shadows collecting in the corners of the room.

Nothing threatening.

Yet your attention keeps returning to them.

Then comes a sound.

Very faint.

A soft scrape somewhere beneath the balcony window.

choices.flavourText: Whatever made the sound does not seem to know whether you have noticed it.

choices.text: Ignore it and leave the room.
choices.flavourText: Whether courage finally wins out, or patience simply runs thin, you step into the corridor.

d05_wait_03.title: A dream
d05_wait_03.text:
The sound comes again.

This time you catch the movement. The curtain beside the balcony shifts, although the doors remain closed and there is still no wind. For a moment there is only darkness beneath the window. Then two long ears rise slowly into the moonlight.

A hare sits beside the curtain.

It should not be here. There is no obvious way it could have entered, yet it seems entirely untroubled by this. Its body is held close and still, every part of it poised between patience and flight.

It watches you.

You watch it.

choices.text: Wait for it to move first.
choices.flavourText: For once, patience is answered.
One long ear turns toward you.

choices.text: Leave it and go into the corridor.
choices.flavourText: At last, waiting becomes harder than moving.

hare_01.title: A dream
hare_01.text:
The hare remains still for another moment, watching with the peculiar attentiveness of something that seems to have been waiting for you specifically. Then it moves closer, one quiet step at a time, crossing the strip of moonlight between you.

Whatever nervous energy had seemed wound through its small body settles as the distance closes. The room seems to soften around it; the edges of the bed, the curtains and the balcony doors lose a little of their certainty. Somewhere far away comes the faint whisper of grass moving beneath a night wind.

The hare lowers its head.

choices.flavourText: Something small and warm settles beneath your hand.

choices.text: Let it come the rest of the way.
choices.flavourText: Patience is answered without ceremony.
The moment passes without protest.

end_hare.title: A dream
end_hare.text:
The instant contact is made, the room falls away.

For one brief moment there is only a pale field beneath an open sky, long grass brushing against your legs and the quick rhythm of a heartbeat that is not entirely your own. Something moves at the edge of sight—fast, light, gone before the eye can settle upon it.

Then you wake.

serpent_01.title: A dream
serpent_01.text:
It is water.

Only a little: a thin dark smear across the polished stone, beading at the edges where the moonlight catches it. There is no overturned vessel nearby, no open window, nothing above that could have dripped. A second mark lies a little farther on, then another.

The trail disappears beneath a narrow archway leading toward one of the palace water courts. You know the fountains there are shut at night.

choices.flavourText: Each mark waits just far enough beyond the last.
The water keeps whatever explanation it has.

serpent_02.title: A dream
serpent_02.text:
The water court is darker than the corridor behind you. Its fountain is silent, the shallow channels around it perfectly still, yet the trail ends at the edge of the central pool.

Something moves beneath the surface.

A long shape turns slowly through the black water, too large to have hidden in so shallow a basin. Scales catch the moonlight one at a time—green, silver, then gone. The serpent rises without disturbing the surface and rests its head upon the stone lip of the pool.

Its tongue tastes the air between you.

choices.text: Lower your hand to the water.
choices.flavourText: Cold gathers around your fingertips before they touch the surface.
The surface closes over the invitation.

end_serpent.title: A dream
end_serpent.text:
The serpent meets your hand at the waterline.

Cold moves beneath your skin—not painful, but deeper than touch has any right to reach. For an instant you become aware of every small thing within yourself: pulse, breath, warmth, the quiet movement of blood through your fingers.

The serpent slips beneath the surface. The water follows it downward, the pool becoming impossibly deep beneath your hand.

Then you wake.

owl_01.title: A dream
owl_01.text:
The city beyond the glass is almost invisible. Roofs and terraces lie beneath the night, their familiar shapes reduced to pale edges among the trees. Above them, however, the sky is unnaturally clear. There are more stars than you remember there being.

A pale shape crosses them.

It moves without a sound, passing close enough to the palace that for an instant broad wings blot out a patch of starlight. The shape rises toward the upper galleries and disappears beyond the roofline.

There is an old stair nearby that leads upward.

choices.flavourText: The movement is gone, but its direction remains.

choices.text: Return your attention to the corridor.
choices.flavourText: The stars offer no explanation.

owl_02.title: A dream
owl_02.text:
The stair ends at a small upper gallery open to the night. Instruments used for charting the heavens stand beneath the arches, their brass rings and narrow arms pale with moonlight. No one has covered them. No one appears to have been here at all.

The owl waits on the highest ring of an old astrolabe.

Its feathers are almost colourless in the dark. It turns its head as you enter, fixing you with two black eyes that seem to hold more of the room than they reflect. For a moment you become aware of details you had not noticed—the tiny scratches in the brass, dust shifting on the floor, something moving far below in the garden.

choices.flavourText: The rest of the gallery seems to sharpen around those two dark eyes.
Some things remain clearer at a distance.

end_owl.title: A dream
end_owl.text:
The owl does not blink.

The gallery brightens without any increase in light. Every edge becomes distinct at once: stone grain, individual leaves far below, the smallest movement beneath the arches. For a breath it feels possible to notice everything, if only you could keep your eyes open long enough.

A wing passes across your vision.

Then you wake.

d06.title: A dream
d06.text:
You continue toward the door that closed at the far end of the hall. With each pool of moonlight crossed, the palace grows a little less certain around you. The right paintings hang in the right places; the pillars are spaced as they should be; even the faint cracks in the stone seem familiar. Yet the distance between one thing and the next feels somehow wrong.

When you finally reach the door, it opens beneath the slightest pressure.

Beyond it, the passage divides where no division should exist. From the left comes the faint rhythm of movement heading toward the training courts. To the right, something small slips through a narrow servants' passage and is gone before you can make out its shape. Straight ahead, the doors to the inner gardens stand open, carrying the cool scent of leaves into the palace.

choices.text: Follow the movement toward the training court.
choices.flavourText: Whatever is ahead is moving with purpose.
The smaller path is the one that should not be here.
Cool air carries the smell of damp earth and leaves.

wolf_01.title: A dream
wolf_01.text:
The passage opens onto one of the training courts. Racks of practice weapons stand beneath the covered walkways, and pale sand fills the square at the centre. No lamps burn. No instructors wait. Nothing here should have been moving.

A wolf stands in the middle of the court.

It is larger than any wolf you have seen depicted, though there is nothing monstrous in its shape. Its breath clouds faintly in the cold air. It does not bare its teeth when you enter. It does not retreat either.

The distance between you feels deliberate.

choices.flavourText: Neither of you gives ground.

choices.text: Stand your ground and let it approach.
choices.flavourText: The wolf watches for a long moment, then begins to move.
The distance remains between you.

end_wolf.title: A dream
end_wolf.text:
The wolf closes the final distance without hurry. Warm breath brushes your hand, followed by the rough press of fur as it lowers its head against you.

The court disappears beneath the sudden smell of rain and pine. For one brief instant you are running through darkness with the ground passing quickly beneath you, every distant sound placed exactly where it belongs. There is another heartbeat beside your own—or perhaps inside it.

Then you wake.

fox_01.title: A dream
fox_01.text:
The narrow passage should lead only to servants' stairs. Instead it turns twice, descends a few steps, then opens into another corridor you do not recognise. The palace has somehow become intimate here: low arches, little doors, corners too close together for any grand procession.

At the far end, something red disappears around a corner.

When you reach it, a fox is waiting. It sits neatly in the middle of the passage, tail curled around its feet. The instant you stop, it rises and trots away again—not fleeing, exactly. Merely assuming you will understand.

choices.flavourText: It never hurries, yet somehow remains just out of reach.

choices.text: Refuse to be led around your own palace.
choices.flavourText: The fox waits at the next corner. When you do not follow, it vanishes.

fox_02.title: A dream
fox_02.text:
The fox leads you through a palace that grows less familiar with every turn. Once you pass through the same doorway twice and emerge somewhere different each time. Another corridor ends in a wall until the fox slips behind a hanging and reveals a passage where there should be solid stone.

At last it stops in a tiny moonlit courtyard no larger than a room. There is nowhere else to go.

The fox sits beneath a small tree and looks back at you. Something in its expression feels dangerously close to amusement.

choices.flavourText: The game, if that is what it was, seems to be over.
Some paths need not be followed to their end.

end_fox.title: A dream
end_fox.text:
The fox rises as you approach and circles once around your feet. Its tail brushes your ankle, impossibly soft.

The courtyard changes between one step and the next. For a heartbeat you stand at the meeting point of a hundred narrow paths, each disappearing into tall grass, stone, woodland or darkness. You cannot explain how, but one of them feels obvious.

The fox takes it without looking back.

Then you wake.

stag_01.title: A dream
stag_01.text:
The inner garden is not as you left it.

The clipped hedges have grown high enough to lose their careful shapes, and grass rises between stones that should have been swept clean. White flowers gather around the dry fountain at the centre. Beyond it, beneath a tree whose branches stretch far wider than the garden should allow, stands a stag.

It is enormous. Not misshapen, not monstrous—simply greater than such a creature ought to be. Its antlers branch upward into the leaves until it is difficult to tell where one ends and the other begins.

The stag lowers its head as you enter the garden.

choices.flavourText: The garden seems to settle around the decision.
Each step feels heavier than the last, but none are refused.

choices.text: Step aside and let it pass.
choices.flavourText: Nothing asks you to follow.

end_stag.title: A dream
end_stag.text:
The stag comes forward.

It stops close enough that the breadth of its antlers fills your vision. For a moment you feel the slow force of its breathing, steady and deep, and beneath that something older: roots beneath soil, sap rising through wood, the patient weight of a living thing that has no need to hurry.

Its brow touches yours.

The garden becomes a forest of white trunks beneath a pale sky.

Then you wake.

end_pure.title: A dream
end_pure.text:
Whatever had been waiting for you makes no attempt to follow.

The palace gathers itself around the absence: familiar stone, pale moonlight, the quiet shape of corridors you have known all your life. For one clear moment the dream feels almost ordinary again. Nothing has been taken from you. Nothing has been added.

Then you wake.
